step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture shows a serverless data processing pipeline for monitoring client Lambda functions. Starting from the top left, a Client Lambda function (node 0) sends logs to a Kinesis Data Stream (node 1). A Transform Lambda function (node 2) consumes log data from this stream, interacts bidirectionally with a DynamoDB table (node 3) to look up customer metadata and keep track of partial invocations, and produces invocation records into a second Kinesis Data Stream (node 4). From this second Kinesis stream, the flow splits into two paths: (1) A storage Lambda (node 5) consumes invocation records and writes them to a Serverless Aurora database (node 6) for rapid single-item querying. (2) Kinesis Data Firehose (node 7) ingests invocation records, uses AWS Glue (node 8) for schema conversion to Parquet format, and writes the transformed files into an S3 data lake bucket (node 9). Finally, Amazon Athena (node 10) queries the aggregated metric data directly from S3. All visual icons and drawn directional arrows are accurately encoded into corresponding nodes and sequence flows.
